record.paper_title: Selected Open Problems in Discrete Geometry and Optimization
record.original_question: Let S_k be a finite set of k-simplices in R^d, with 1 <= k <= d - 2. Suppose S_k satisfies the same antipodal-support property as in the segment problem: for every two distinct simplices, there are distinct parallel supporting hyperplanes of the convex hull of the union of all simplices in S_k, with one simplex contained in one supporting hyperplane and the other contained in the other. Must |S_k| <= 2^(d-k)?

evidence.quote: Of course, more generally, we may consider a set Sk of k-simplices in Rd, which satisfy the word-for-word analogue of the above property. Is it true, that then |Sk| <= 2d-k? Here 1 <= k <= d - 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix integers $d \ge 3$ and $k$ with $1 \le k \le d-2$. Let $S_k = \{T_1, \dots, T_n\}$ be a finite collection of $k$-dimensional simplices in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and let $C = \mathrm{conv}\bigl(\bigcup_{i=1}^n T_i\bigr)$ denote the convex hull of their union. A hyperplane $H \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ is called a supporting hyperplane of $C$ if $H \cap C \neq \emptyset$ and $C$ lies entirely in one of the two closed half-spaces bounded by $H$. Assume that $S_k$ has the following antipodal property: for every pair of distinct indices $i \neq j$, there exist two distinct parallel supporting hyperplanes $H'$ and $H''$ of $C$ such that $T_i \subset H'$ and $T_j \subset H''$.

Prove or disprove: under these hypotheses, $|S_k| \le 2^{d-k}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is the Makai–Martini conjecture, generalizing the Danzer–Grünbaum theorem (which is the case k=0) and the segment case k=1. The bound $2^{d-k}$ is known to be sharp (attained by the $2^{d-k}$ parallel $k$-faces of a $d$-cube). Recent work has produced lower-bound constructions and partial upper bounds, but the conjecture as stated appears to remain open in general.

status_evidence.title: On the number of antipodal or strictly antipodal pairs...
status_evidence.snippet: Makai and Martini conjectured that a k-antipodal set of k-simplices in R^d has at most 2^(d-k) elements, with equality for the parallel k-faces of a cube.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is attributed to Makai and Martini and the bound is sharp.

status_evidence.title: Large antipodal families
status_evidence.snippet: Work on lower-bound constructions for strictly antipodal (k-1)-simplices addressing questions of Makai and Martini.
status_evidence.claim: Active research provides constructions and partial results, but the upper-bound conjecture is not established in general.
